section: Raja Rammohan Roy and the Brahmo Samaj; abolition of Sati; Debendranath and Keshab Chandra Sen
subsections: Maharashtra reform - Prarthana Samaj, Bombay/Poona reformers, National Social Conference

accepted.s: Prarthana Samaj was established in which year?
accepted.x: Prarthana Samaj was established in 1867. It became an important reformist organisation in Maharashtra.
accepted.tq: Use the numerical options to distinguish the founding year from nearby reform milestones.
accepted.sec: Maharashtra reform - Prarthana Samaj, Bombay/Poona reformers, National Social Conference  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following reforms was NOT associated with the activities of the Prarthana Samaj?
o: Use of violent confrontation against orthodox groups
accepted.x: Prarthana Samaj promoted widow remarriage, women's education and inter-caste dining through persuasion rather than confrontation. Violent confrontation was not its method.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the organisation's method of gradual persuasion.
accepted.sec: Maharashtra reform - Prarthana Samaj, Bombay/Poona reformers, National Social Conference  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the leadership of Prarthana Samaj:
1. Mahadev Govind Ranade was associated with it.
2. R.G. Bhandarkar was associated with it.
3. Both were advocates of reform through persuasion rather than confrontation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar were important leaders of Prarthana Samaj, whose reformist approach relied on persuasion. All three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Combine the leadership and method statements and check whether all belong to the same reformist approach.
accepted.sec: Maharashtra reform - Prarthana Samaj, Bombay/Poona reformers, National Social Conference  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Balshastri Jambhekar was associated with Darpan, Karsandas Mulji with Satya Prakash, and Gopal Hari Deshmukh was known as Lokahitawadi. Therefore, all the pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Start from a sure newspaper–reformer pair and verify the remaining associations.
accepted.sec: Maharashtra reform - Prarthana Samaj, Bombay/Poona reformers, National Social Conference  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
With reference to Mahadev Govind Ranade, consider the following statements:
1. He was associated with the Widow Marriage Association.
2. He was associated with the Deccan Education Society.
3. He founded the National Social Conference in 1887 with Raghunath Rao.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Ranade was associated with the Widow Marriage Association and the Deccan Education Society, and founded the National Social Conference in 1887 with Raghunath Rao.
accepted.tq: Test the reformer's several institutional associations together rather than relying on a single name match.
accepted.sec: Maharashtra reform - Prarthana Samaj, Bombay/Poona reformers, National Social Conference  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The National Social Conference founded by M.G. Ranade and Raghunath Rao functioned as:
o: The political wing of the Deccan Education Society
The educational wing of the Prarthana Samaj
The military wing of the Congress
The social wing of the Congress sessions
accepted.x: The National Social Conference was founded in 1887 as the social wing of the Congress sessions.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional role rather than confusing it with the organisation's founders.
accepted.sec: Maharashtra reform - Prarthana Samaj, Bombay/Poona reformers, National Social Conference  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The followers of Henry Vivian Derozio were popularly known as:
accepted.x: The followers of Derozio were known as Derozians.
accepted.tq: Test the exact label used for the followers of a reform leader.
accepted.sec: Young Bengal Movement - leader, Academic Association, ideas  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Academic Association established in 1828 was primarily a forum for:
accepted.x: The Academic Association was established in 1828 as a forum for debate and discussion among the followers of Young Bengal.
accepted.tq: Match the organisation with its precise function instead of a neighbouring social reform activity.
accepted.sec: Young Bengal Movement - leader, Academic Association, ideas  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the ideas of the Young Bengal Movement?
o: Radical rationalism and criticism of social orthodoxy
Opposition to women's education and rights
Exclusive loyalty to idol worship and caste hierarchy
Revival of decadent customs without criticism
accepted.x: Young Bengal stood for radical rationalism, opposed idol worship, casteism and decadent customs, and supported women's rights and education.
accepted.tq: Select the option that combines the movement's intellectual and social objectives.
accepted.sec: Young Bengal Movement - leader, Academic Association, ideas  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Henry Vivian Derozio:
1. He was a teacher at Hindu College, Calcutta.
2. He was removed from Hindu College in 1831.
3. He died in the same year in which he was removed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Derozio taught at Hindu College, was removed in 1831 and died in that same year. All three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Check the linked date statements together, especially the same-year relationship.
accepted.sec: Young Bengal Movement - leader, Academic Association, ideas  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who was the first Andhra associated with the Brahmo Samaj?
accepted.x: Mannava Buchayya Pantulu is identified as the first Andhra associated with the Brahmo Samaj.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first Andhra associate from the later Andhra Trinity and organisational promoters.
accepted.sec: Brahmo Samaj in Andhra - Veeresalingam, Venkataratnam Naidu  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Madras Veda Samajam was renamed as the Dakshina Bharatha Desa Brahmo Samajam under the leadership of:
accepted.x: The Madras Veda Samajam was renamed the Dakshina Bharatha Desa Brahmo Samajam under Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu.
accepted.tq: Use the organisation–leader association and avoid confusing it with the Andhra Brahmo Trinity.
accepted.sec: Brahmo Samaj in Andhra - Veeresalingam, Venkataratnam Naidu  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Veeresalingam's Prarthana Samaj in Rajahmundry was established in:
accepted.x: Veeresalingam's Prarthana Samaj was established at Rajahmundry in 1878.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the four Andhra reform dates by linking each year with its place and organiser.
accepted.sec: Brahmo Samaj in Andhra - Veeresalingam, Venkataratnam Naidu  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu — Prarthana Samaj, Rajahmundry, 1888
accepted.x: Venkataratnam Naidu established a Brahmo Samaj at Machilipatnam in 1882. The other options incorrectly interchange the organisers, places or years.
accepted.tq: Check the organiser, location and year as a three-part match.
accepted.sec: Brahmo Samaj in Andhra - Veeresalingam, Venkataratnam Naidu  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Andhra Brahmo-related developments in chronological order:
A. Veeresalingam's Prarthana Samaj at Rajahmundry
B. Venkataratnam Naidu's Brahmo Samaj at Machilipatnam
C. Brahmo Samaj at Kakinada
D. Brahmo Samaj at Guntur
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Rajahmundry in 1878, Machilipatnam in 1882, Kakinada in 1888 and Guntur in 1898.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the two middle developments.
accepted.sec: Brahmo Samaj in Andhra - Veeresalingam, Venkataratnam Naidu  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the Brahmo Trinity of Andhra?
o: Mannava Buchayya Pantulu, M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar
Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu, Balshastri Jambhekar and Gopal Hari Deshmukh
Henry Vivian Derozio, Veeresalingam and Karsandas Mulji
Veeresalingam, Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu and Desiraju Peda Bapaiah
accepted.x: The Brahmo Trinity of Andhra comprised Veeresalingam, Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu and Desiraju Peda Bapaiah.
accepted.tq: Separate a regional collective title from individual founders and leaders of other reform movements.
accepted.sec: Brahmo Samaj in Andhra - Veeresalingam, Venkataratnam Naidu  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Brahmo Samaj from the Arya Samaj?
o: The Brahmo Samaj was revivalist, whereas the Arya Samaj rejected all religious traditions.
The Brahmo Samaj was reformist and based on reason and modern ideas, whereas the Arya Samaj was revivalist.
Both were exclusively political organisations with no social reform programme.
Both opposed education and women's rights.
accepted.x: The Brahmo Samaj is characterised as a reformist movement stressing reason and modern ideas, while the Arya Samaj is treated as revivalist.
accepted.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap by checking which movement is reformist and which is revivalist.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Brahmo Samaj and Prarthana Samaj had which of the following in common?
o: Both followed a reformist approach based on reason.
Both were founded as military organisations.
accepted.x: Brahmo Samaj and Prarthana Samaj were reformist movements that emphasised reason and social reform.
accepted.tq: Identify the common feature while rejecting options that reverse their reformist character.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs represents revivalist movements rather than reformist movements?
accepted.x: Arya Samaj and Deoband are classified as revivalist movements, whereas Brahmo Samaj and Prarthana Samaj are reformist.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the paired categories of reformist and revivalist movements.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following statements best expresses the broader significance of the Brahmo Samaj?
o: It confined its activities entirely to ritual worship.
It attacked superstition, promoted education and women's rights, and helped create the base for nationalism.
It sought to preserve caste restrictions without modification.
It opposed modern education and social reform.
accepted.x: The Brahmo Samaj opposed superstition, supported education and women's rights, and contributed to the intellectual and social foundations of nationalism.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that captures the movement's multiple social and national consequences.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which region is regarded as the first Indian region to experience a renaissance?
accepted.x: Bengal is identified as the first Indian region to experience a renaissance. Within Andhra, Rajahmundry is associated with the first renaissance.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the all-India regional first from the corresponding Andhra location.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: In the context of the Andhra renaissance, which place is identified as its centre?
accepted.x: Rajahmundry is identified as the place associated with the first renaissance in Andhra.
accepted.tq: Separate the Andhra-specific first from the later Brahmo Samaj centres and dates.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations associated with Raja Rammohan Roy is correctly matched?
o: Atmiya Sabha — association connected with his reform activities
accepted.x: Raja Rammohan Roy's reform profile includes the Atmiya Sabha, Vedanta College established in 1825 and the abolition of Sati in 1829.
accepted.tq: Verify the three related reform milestones before selecting the inclusive option.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT listed among the broader demands associated with Raja Rammohan Roy?
o: Permanent military rule by the East India Company
accepted.x: Rammohan Roy was associated with reform, peasant concerns and administrative demands; permanent military rule by the East India Company was not among these demands.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme political option that is unrelated to the reformer's documented agenda.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Raja Rammohan Roy was profiled in the PMF IAS LENS feature of May 2026 primarily in connection with:
o: Sati, Atmiya Sabha, Vedanta College and his wider reform demands
The formation of the Indian National Army
The founding of the Deccan Education Society
accepted.x: The May 2026 profile highlighted Rammohan Roy's role in the campaign against Sati, the Atmiya Sabha, Vedanta College and his peasant and administrative demands.
accepted.tq: Use the current-affairs framing to identify the complete cluster of associated themes.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Rabindranath Tagore, remembered in the cited anniversary reference, was the youngest son of which Brahmo leader?
accepted.x: Rabindranath Tagore was the youngest son of Debendranath Tagore, a leader of the Brahmo movement.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the family relationship from the other named Brahmo and Maharashtra reformers.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
